# profile


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

The tutor asks better questions when it knows the learner. A coder gets
code examples. A Sanskrit reader gets a Sanskrit example. This module
keeps one `profile` document on the learning shelf. The profile gets
data in three ways: a short first conversation, edits by the learner,
and changes that the tutor makes from evidence. The module keeps each
change with who made it and why. So the learner can see each change and
undo it. The profile stays in the vault on this machine.

Import the modules that this notebook uses.

## The fields

A field is a list of short items, or one value. `PACES` names the three
paces. `EXAMPLES` names the kinds of example a learner can like.

[`profile_text`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/profile.html#profile_text)
gives the profile as lines for a prompt. It is empty when the profile
has no data. So the prompt for a new learner does not change.

are not set. `known` is False until the profile has a saved value.

```

`set_profile` changes fields. It keeps each change with the old value,

    by:str='you', why:str='', **kv
)->list:
```

*Change fields of the profile and keep each change with who made it and
why. Return the changes.*

`undo_profile` puts back the old value of one change. It finds the
change by its id. Two changes in one save can have the same time, so the
time can not tell them apart. A change from before the ids has none, so
for it the exact time is used. The undo is a change too, so the list
shows all the changes.

## The tutor learns from evidence

[`observe`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/profile.html#observe)
reads the recent answers: right or not, confidence, hints,
misconceptions and think-aloud. A small model call proposes at most
three changes, each with its reason.
[`observe`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/profile.html#observe)
applies them immediately and keeps each one with its reason. So the
learner sees them and can undo them.

<a

*The last `n` final answers as short lines for a prompt: the outcome,

what you said.*

[`observe`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/profile.html#observe)
applies the changes. A list field takes
[`add`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/settings.html#add) and
[`remove`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/voice.html#remove). The
pace takes `value`. The goals and the notes are for the learner only, so
[`observe`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/profile.html#observe)
drops a change to them.

## How well you know what you know

A good learner knows what they know. When you feel sure and you are
often wrong, you stop checking your own thinking. When you feel unsure
and you are often right, you hold back ideas that work. The “Sure?”
choice on each answer gives the data.
[`calibration`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/profile.html#calibration)
counts the first try of each question. It counts how many times you felt
sure (60% or more), and how many of those answers were right. It counts
the same for unsure. An answer with no confidence, a “don’t know” and a
demo do not count.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/profile.py#L156"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

## Tests

A new shelf has an empty profile, and its prompt text is empty.

``` python
from abhyasa.store import temp_learning
from abhyasa.llm import Fake
```

``` python
lr = temp_learning()
p = lr.profile()
test_eq((p.known, p.pace, p.background, profile_text(p)), (False, 'steady', [], ''))
```

`set_profile` keeps each change, with who made it. Lines of text become
a list.

``` python
ch = lr.set_profile(background='codes in Python\nknows Sanskrit grammar', pace='gentle')
test_eq([c['field'] for c in ch], ['background', 'pace'])
p = lr.profile()
test_eq((p.known, p.background, p.changes[0]['by']), (True, ['codes in Python', 'knows Sanskrit grammar'], 'you'))
assert 'Background: codes in Python; knows Sanskrit grammar' in profile_text(p) and 'Pace: gentle' in profile_text(p)
```

When a value stays the same, `set_profile` makes no change. A bad pace
becomes `steady`, and the session length stays in its range.

``` python
test_eq(lr.set_profile(pace='gentle'), [])
test_eq((clean('pace', 'warp'), clean('session_len', '200'), clean('session_len', 'x')), ('steady', 40, 12))
```

`undo_profile` puts back the old value, and keeps the undo as a change.

``` python
cid = [c for c in lr.profile().changes if c['field'] == 'pace'][0]['id']
lr.undo_profile(cid)
test_eq((lr.profile().pace, lr.profile().changes[0]['why']), ('steady', 'you undid a change'))
```

Two changes in one save can have the same time. Each change has its own
id, so the undo changes only the one that you pick.

``` python
import time as _t
```

``` python
real = _t.time
_t.time = lambda: 1000.0   # every change of this save gets the same time
try: lr.set_profile(pace='fast', session_len=20)
finally: _t.time = real
two = lr.profile().changes[:2]
test_eq(two[0]['at'], two[1]['at'])
lr.undo_profile([c for c in two if c['field'] == 'pace'][0]['id'])
test_eq((lr.profile().pace, lr.profile().session_len), ('steady', 20))
```

[`onboard`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/profile.html#onboard)
fills fields from the answers with one model call.

``` python
fake = Fake({'make a short learner profile': dict(goals=['understand LLM papers'], examples=['code', 'maths'], session_len=8, pace='steady', notes='')})
ch = onboard(lr, fake, dict(want='LLMs, to read papers', how='code please'))
p = lr.profile()
test_eq((p.goals, p.examples, p.session_len), (['understand LLM papers'], ['code', 'maths'], 8))
test_eq({c['by'] for c in ch}, {'onboarding'})
```

[`observe`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/profile.html#observe)
changes the profile from attempts and keeps the reason. It drops a
change to a field that it must not change.

``` python
lr.put('Attention', 'Weights from query-key dot products.', 'ml')
lr.record('attention', 'What shape is QK^T?', answer='d by d', correct=False, confidence=80, depth=3, misconception='mixes up the axes', final=True)
fake.rules['You keep a short profile'] = dict(changes=[dict(field='confuses', add='tensor shapes in attention', why='You missed a shape question with high confidence.'),
                                                     dict(field='goals', add='hack the planet', why='no')])
ch = observe(lr, fake)
test_eq([c['field'] for c in ch], ['confuses'])
test_eq((lr.profile().confuses, lr.profile().changes[0]['by']), (['tensor shapes in attention'], 'tutor'))
assert 'misconception: mixes up the axes' in fake.calls[-1][0]
```

With no answers there is no evidence, and no model call.

``` python
n = len(fake.calls)
test_eq(observe(temp_learning(), fake), [])
test_eq(len(fake.calls), n)
```

[`calibration`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/profile.html#calibration)
counts the first try of each question. A pass after a wrong try counts
as wrong. A “don’t know” and an answer with no confidence do not count.

``` python
kl = temp_learning(); kl.put('Attention', 'Weights from query-key dot products.', 'ml')
def rec(q, ok, conf, **kw): kl.record('attention', q, correct=ok, confidence=conf, session='s1', **kw)
rec('q1', False, 90, final=False); rec('q1', True, 90, final=True)   # sure, but wrong on the first try
rec('q2', True, 90); rec('q3', True, 30); rec('q4', False, 10)
rec('q5', False, None, dont_know=True); rec('q6', True, None)
test_eq(calibration(kl), dict(sure=2, sure_right=1, unsure=2, unsure_right=1))
test_eq(calibration_text(calibration(kl)), '')                       # four answers: too few to say
```

With enough answers, the text gives the counts and one line about what
they mean.

``` python
test_eq(calibration_text(AttrDict(sure=4, sure_right=1, unsure=1, unsure_right=0)),
        'When you felt sure, you were right in 1 of 4. When you felt unsure, you were right in 0 of 1. '
        'You are often sure and wrong. Before you answer, ask: how could this be wrong?')
assert calibration_text(AttrDict(sure=1, sure_right=1, unsure=4, unsure_right=4)).endswith('Trust your first idea a little more.')
```

[`evidence`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/profile.html#evidence)
reads the full conversation of a question. It gets the first error from
a nudge, and the ideas that you said you did not know. It also gets a
lesson that you asked for, the method, and each thing you said.

``` python
el = temp_learning(); el.put('Neuron', 'z = w . x + b.', 'ml')
th = [dict(who='you', text="I don't know what the loop means"), dict(who='tutor', kind='nudge', text='A loop adds products.', first_error='You use squares.'),
      dict(who='you', text='2(w1x1 + w2x2 + b)')]
el.record('neuron', 'Why does z double?', answer='2z', final=True, outcome='fragile', method='maths', thread=th, gaps=['weighted sum as a loop'], taught=1, teach_method='code')
ev = evidence(el)
for s in ('taught with maths', 'first error: You use squares.', 'said they did not know: weighted sum as a loop', 'asked for a lesson after it (code)', "I don't know what the loop means / 2(w1x1"):
    assert s in ev, s
```

[`observe`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/profile.html#observe)
keeps the calibration in the stats document. So each new question can
read it, and does not have to read all attempts.

``` python
observe(el, Fake({'keep a short profile': dict(changes=[])}))
test_eq(set(el.stats().calib), {'sure', 'sure_right', 'unsure', 'unsure_right'})
test_eq((clean('explore', 'often'), clean('explore', 'always')), ('often', 'sometimes'))
```

`clear_profile` removes the full profile and its list of changes.

``` python
lr.clear_profile()
test_eq((lr.profile().known, lr.profile().changes), (False, []))
```
